# ADR-0002: Parser generated by goyacc from a .y grammar derived from the normative grammar; grammar-differential CI; error-code binding at parse time

## Status
Accepted (owner, 2026-11-01 — ratified with the enforcement conditions implemented in ADR-0015 and docs/development/qa-strategy.md).

**Amended 2026-11-04 (owner decision at S2.1, after an evidence spike: [participle-spike.md](../../language/research/participle-spike.md)).** The parser is **participle v2** (struct-tag recursive descent, `github.com/alecthomas/participle/v2` v2.1.4, MIT), not goyacc. Decisions 1 and 2 (the `.y` grammar and its conflict-free build) and the `freshness` note for `parser_gen.go` no longer apply; the `golang.org/x/tools` dependency is not added. Decision 3 stands as written, except that the keyword table is pinned equal to `grammar.lark`'s NAME exclusion list by a test rather than generated by `tools/kwgen/`. Decision 4 stands: every [parse] code is reachable with line, column and fix text, through an error map over participle's error (the unexpected token, its context and the expected set). Decision 5, the grammar differential on verdicts **and parse shapes** (S2.2a), is the equivalence proof for the Go side, which has no conflict analysis of its own; the spike showed the grammar deterministic at lookahead 1. Decision 6 stands.

## Context
The spec's grammar ([docs/language/grammar.lark](../../language/grammar.lark)) is normative, machine-checked (LALR conflict-free = the unambiguity proof), and frozen. The engine needs a Go parser that accepts exactly the same language. The tooling research ([docs/language/research/grammar-tooling.md](../../language/research/grammar-tooling.md)) rejected PEG (hides ambiguity by ordered choice), ANTLR (silent ambiguity resolution + Java build dep), and participle (no conflict analysis), and recommended goyacc — LALR(1) with conflict reporting, precedented by CockroachDB, Vitess and PromQL. Deploy-time errors must carry line/col and one of the 23 parse-level codes in [docs/language/errors.md](../../language/errors.md) (SPEC §7).

## Decision
1. The engine parser is generated by `goyacc` from `internal/parser/cep.y`. The `.y` grammar is hand-derived from `grammar.lark`, construct for construct, with a header comment mapping every production to its lark counterpart by name.
2. The goyacc build MUST report **zero shift/reduce and zero reduce/reduce conflicts**; the gate runs the generator and fails on any conflict (same proof obligation as the lark side).
3. A hand-written lexer (`internal/parser/lexer.go`) implements SPEC §2 exactly: lowercase-only keywords; the reserved-word table shared with the validator as **one data file** `internal/parser/keywords.go` generated from `grammar.lark`'s NAME exclusion list by `tools/kwgen/` (the gate regenerates and diffs — drift fails); E-KW-001/E-KW-002 distinction (any-case reserved vs non-lowercase keyword spelling); raw triple-quoted strings; one-line single-quoted strings (E-STR-001); the exhaustive escape set (E-STR-002 at validation); BOM ignored; `--` and `/* */` comments (unterminated block = E-CMT-001).
4. Parse errors are produced through a custom `yyError` path that maps parser states to catalog codes: every code marked **[parse]** in errors.md MUST be reachable and MUST carry line, column, and the catalog's fix text. A table-driven test feeds every file in `docs/language/invalid/` and asserts the exact expected code from the file's first-line comment.
5. **Grammar-differential job (T4):** a gate step runs the Python checker (`grammar_check.py` with `grammar.lark`) AND the Go parser over the full corpus — the Python side is PINNED like every gate tool (round-2 F18): `tools.json` records the Python version and `lark==1.3.1` with checksums; the gate's installer builds the venv; the checker script is repo-tracked (`.claude/skills/language-design/scripts/`, committed) — `docs/language/examples/`, `docs/language/invalid/`, `docs/language/eval/generated/` — *and, from sprint S11, `gallery/` (annotated 2026-11-02: the attack-gallery rule files join the differential corpus)* — and fails on any accept/reject disagreement. **Amended 2026-11-01 (pre-mortem RC7, dispositioned via the foundation consistency review S12):** verdict agreement alone cannot catch a precedence or associativity divergence that still accepts, so the differential also compares **parse shapes**: both sides emit a canonical **operator-spine S-expression** per accepted file (nested unary/binary applications with operator names, plus leaf kinds `name|literal` — positions and token text excluded; the mapping is defined once in `tools/grammar-diff.md`, produced by a lark post-pass on one side and a Go AST walker on the other) and the step byte-diffs them; plus ≥ 10 precedence/associativity **torture files** under `docs/language/eval/generated/torture/` (count asserted by the step's expected scope). This lands with the differential in S2. This is the standing equivalence proof between the normative grammar and the engine.
6. The parser produces an AST (`internal/parser/ast.go`) that is lowered in a separate file (`lower.go`) to `internal/model` — the AST never escapes `internal/parser`.

## Alternatives considered
- **Hand-written recursive descent** — rejected for v0.1: no machine conflict check; the LALR proof is the point. (The error-message layer is hand-written anyway; we get precision where it matters without giving up the proof.)
- **ANTLR4 Go target / participle / pigeon** — rejected in the tooling research for ambiguity-concealment and no-conflict-analysis reasons; see that document for citations.
- **Generating the .y from grammar.lark mechanically** — deferred: a transpiler is its own project; the differential job gives equivalent assurance at corpus strength, and the kwgen tool removes the most drift-prone part (the keyword list).

## Consequences
- Positive: conflict-free LALR on both sides; corpus-level equivalence continuously enforced; error codes tested 1:1 against counter-files.
- Negative: two grammars to maintain (lark normative, .y derived) — mitigated by the differential job and kwgen; goyacc ergonomics are dated — accepted, the grammar is small (<60 effective productions).
- Dependency added (owner sign-off required): `golang.org/x/tools` pinned, **build-time only** (generated parser is committed; users never need goyacc).

## Implementation notes for coding agents
- Commit the generated `y.go` (named `internal/parser/parser_gen.go`) so `go build` needs no generator; the gate regenerates and diffs to catch stale commits.
- Lexer keywords: match longest-identifier first, then look up the lowercase form in the keyword table; if found and spelling is exactly lowercase → keyword token; if found case-insensitively but not lowercase → E-KW-002 error token; else NAME.
- Position tracking: the lexer counts lines/columns in runes; every token carries `Pos{Line, Col}`; the AST nodes carry the Pos of their first token.
- Duration literals are lexed as NUMBER + unit tokens and assembled by the grammar; integer-ness/descending/distinct checks are E-DUR-002 in the validator, not the lexer (grammar stays equivalent to lark).
